questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: One of my good friends went on exchange in Prague a year before me, and she had an amazing time, so i knew it would be a good experience for me as well. I knew i wanted to stay in Europe, but still explore a culture that i did not know a lot about beforehand. I also wanted to be able to make trips to other countries during my exchange and there are a lot of places to visit from the starting point of Prague. Apart from that the cost of living in Czech Republic is much lower than in Denmark, so i knew that i would be able to have a lot of nice experiences and delicious food without worrying too much about money.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was quite easy and the questions I had were answered quickly by email. They were quite late with distributing the dates of the start of the semester etc, but i recieved it eventually.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Charles University organized an introduction week for all the international students with both an introduction to the system of the school as well as a small city tour where they showed us how to get student ID, transportation tickets etc...

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very hard to find housing off campus. I found an apartment shared with 7 other international students via facebook, but I heard about a lot of people who got scammed, so you have to be careful. But I really recommend finding a shared apartment off campus! Its an easy way of finding friends without much effort and its a really nice community to be a part of! I am really happy I chose this solution its where i found some of my best friends during the stay.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The dorms are located around the city, but the ones connected to the faculty of humanities are right next to the school. So living off campus is a nice way of getting to know the city and different neighborhoods since you naturally have to move around to get to school. Furthermore the dorms are often located a bit far from the city center, so sometimes it can be a long way home. The dorms are also very old and worn, you have to share a room with another person and the kitchens are tiny and not equipped at all. The only pro about the dorms is that its very cheap.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a little bit difficult because the system is very old, but once you get the hang of it its pretty easy. We had a 2-week add and drop period so we could test out classes before finally choosing them which was really nice. But it also ended up being a bit stressfull because courses got filled quickly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The university was very good at helping whenever i had questions and its always possible to ask teachers or the international office if you have questions,

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted, so i was pretty sucessful, but it was a big puzzle trying to make all the classes fit with the 30 ECTS points required since a lot of the classes are 2,3,4,5,6 points each.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try a lot of classes in the add and drop period! Some of the classes i though would be most interesting from the descriptions i ended up dropping and vice versa. And also check out classes from other faculties they have some really interesting ones! But beware of the different registration dates for the different faculties

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had some BA and some MA courses and therefore the academic level of the courses also varied a bit, but i think the overall level was alright.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I did not really have any lectures, mostly seminars which i enjoyed, but the style of teaching is more old school and attendance is mandatory in all classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Medical Anthropology: Illness, Medicine and the Body
Body, Affect and Society
Observing the city: Introduction to fieldwork in an urban environment
Gender and Religion
Feminism, Art & Pop Culture
Iconology: Art-historical and Philosophical Aspects Of Reading The Cultural Phenomena

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: My two favorite courses were Medical Anthropology and Observing the city. Medical Anthropology was a really interesting class with a nice syllabus and a very professional teacher. I really enjoyed this course even though it is a bit more work. Observing the city was also very interesting. We went on fieldwork in 3 different locations in Prague which was a very nice way of getting to know the city as well as Czech culture. The teacher in this course was also very nice and well prepared for each class.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not have a lot of unexpected costs, but i did have to pay a booking fee of approx 1300 DKK apart from the deposit on my shared apartment

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food, drinks, and experiences like the cinema, bowling, museums etc was cheaper than expected. General rent prices and grocery shopping was more expensive than i had anticipated.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In the beginning there were some social activities organized by the university, but after the first weeks the students organized things by themselves. Outside there are groups like ESN and other firms/communities organizing a lot of events and experiences for erasmus students, so it was not a problem that the university did not organize that much.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of nice, museums, monuments, parks, restaurants, bars, cafes, clubs, vintage stores and so on to explore as well as small cities in the rest of Czech republic you can visit.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on weekend trips to ex Budapest, Vienna, Berlin etc with your friends! there are a lot of cheap busses and trains going from the central train or bus station.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Since its a european country it was pretty easy. One that surprised me was the fact that the service in restaurants etc is very rude and some places they refuse to speak english, but most people are nice enough. And they have a lot of special traditions which are fun to explore.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Unfortunately i mostly socialized with other exchange students. The Czech students kept a lot to themselves and were a bit hard to get in contact with, maybe because of the language barrier. I think a good idea for getting to know more Czech students is getting a buddy through the system at the university.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Czech republic is a very homogenic country and they dont have many immigrants, so this was different from Copenhagen. Otherwise I did not encounter a lot of challenges.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The city is very beautiful and if you seek out the right restaurants the local food can be quite good! Czech republic has a very interesting history which is worth diving into. And they really love cheap beer.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Find a shared apartment with other exchange students, it is really a great way of meeting people right away when you arrive and a good way to prevent feeling lonely in a foreign country. Enjoy that eating out, going to bars and all the other stuff you can do is a lot cheaper than back home, use it to its fullest. This is also where you meet new friends and learn about the culture. Always make sure that you have some cash, even though a lot of places take cards most bars for example only take cash.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The people at the university are always happy to help, so dont hesitate with asking questions. The faculty of humanities is located a bit far out from the city center, so if you want to study in the center of the city take classes from other faculties as well. And use some of the many beautiful libraries in the city.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people and living with people from all over the world. Exploring the city and all the possibilities that it holds!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Probably the language barrier sometimes and figuring out what classes to take. But fortunately I did not have a lot of challenges

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
